text: "The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong… but time and chance happen to them all." Only God can put you at the right place at the right time.
explanation:
The wisest man who ever lived observed that the fastest don't always win, the skilled don't always get the favour, and the smartest don't always get rich. What makes the difference is being in the right place at the right time: meeting an old friend who just happens to need someone like you, or arriving just when a door opens.

No amount of cleverness can arrange that. Only God can, whether it's opening an opportunity or steering you away from a tragedy you never knew was ahead. That's why it's better to trust in the Lord than to put confidence in man. Ask Him to order your timing.

text: Chronos is time on the clock. Kairos is the right time: the opportune, favourable moment. God has kairos moments for you.
explanation:
The Greek Old Testament translates the "time" of Ecclesiastes 9:11 with kairos. Chronos measures time in numbers: one o'clock, ten years. Kairos describes time by its quality: a seasonable, opportune moment, the time when something is ripe.

Peter promised that when people turn to God, "times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord." Those times are kairos too. Not every day will feel like one, but as you stay in His presence, expect seasons of refreshing and moments that open up in a way only He could arrange.

text: The Hebrew word for the right time first appears when the dove returned to Noah "in the evening," with a fresh olive leaf in her mouth.
explanation:
By the law of first mention, the first time a word appears in Scripture often sets its meaning. The first use of et, the Hebrew for a right or opportune time, is when the dove comes back to the ark, and Noah knows the judgment is over and the waters have receded.

The dove is a picture of the Holy Spirit. He's the One who orchestrates events and circumstances to put you in the right place at the right time. So learn to listen for His inner green light and His peace before you sign, decide or commit, in small things as well as big ones. You're not stepping into the year alone.

text: "In due season we shall reap if we do not lose heart." Due season is kairos. If you've waited long, don't faint now.
explanation:
Abraham and Sarah waited over twenty years. Then the Lord said, "I will return to you according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son." When Paul quoted it in Romans, the word for that appointed time was kairos. "Is anything too hard for the Lord?" can be read, "Is anything too wonderful for Him?"

You may have been believing God for something for years with only small improvements. The timing of the harvest is His, but the promise is sure. Don't grow weary. And when your kairos comes, Paul adds, "as we have opportunity" (kairos again), "let us do good to all."

text: Ruth said, "Let me glean after him in whose sight I shall find grace." Then "her hap was to light" on the field of Boaz.
explanation:
Ruth was a Moabite widow in a strange town, with only the most back-breaking work open to her. By the law she was disqualified, but she set out expecting grace. And of all the fields in Bethlehem, she "happened" to come to the part belonging to Boaz, a wealthy, unmarried relative of her late husband, a picture of Jesus our Redeemer.

The old King James says, "her hap was to light," and both words come from the Hebrew karah: a right happening. Grace and right happenings go together. You can't engineer it. You can only trust His favour and say, "I will find grace."

text: "Son, I delayed this flight just for you."
explanation:
Years ago, Joseph Prince and his wife misread their departure time and arrived at the airport with a two-year-old, three bags and a pram after check-in had closed. They ran the length of the terminal, frustrated with each other and themselves, and made it onto the plane. Then came the announcement: a faulty conveyor belt was holding up departure. As he sat wondering who was delaying the flight, the Lord spoke: "Son, I delayed this flight just for you."

Every bit of stress melted. Not everything that happens is good, but if you're God's child, "all things work together for good." Sometimes the delay you're frustrated by is His hand holding the door open for you.

text: Abraham's servant prayed, "Give me success this day, and show kindness to my master." Before he had finished speaking, Rebekah came out.
explanation:
This is the first occurrence of karah, the word for a right happening, and here it's translated "success." It's paired with chesed: grace, kindness. Many young women came to the well in the evening, yet the one who appeared was Rebekah, who offered water to a stranger and his ten thirsty camels.

God had set it in motion before the servant even prayed. "Before they call, I will answer; and while they are still speaking, I will hear." Pray his prayer this week: "Lord, give me success today; show me Your grace." Then watch for it, and give Jesus the glory.
